chunks: To those who do wrong out of ignorance, then repent and correct themselves, your Lord is indeed forgiving and kind.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for God's forgiveness for those who sin out of ignorance?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked with its preceding verse (16:118) to distinguish between sins committed out of genuine ignorance versus those done with full knowledge, emphasizing that sincere repentance (tawbah) and moral rectification (islah) are prerequisites for divine mercy. It underscores the concept of 'Ghafur' (all-forgiving) and 'Rahim' (all-merciful) as active divine attributes that respond to the believer's return, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the accessibility of God's forgiveness for those who correct their conduct.
